item.title: Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in work, is devoted to delight in work; delights in talking, takes pleasure in talking, is devoted to delight in talking; delights in sleeping, takes pleasure in sleeping, is devoted to delight in sleeping.

A bhikkhu who delights in work,
Delights in talking,
Delights in sleeping,
Is restless and agitated.
Such a bhikkhu cannot attain
Supreme enlightenment.

Therefore, let him have few duties,
Little sleep, no restlessness,
Such a bhikkhu can attain
Supreme enlightenment.

From: Itivuttaka 79

item.title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with such…
item.description:
Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with such robes as he receives here and there; is content with such almsfood as he receives here and there; is content with such lodgings as he receives here and there; is content with such medicinal requisites as he receives here and there; and he dwells with many thoughts of renunciation. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.127

item.title: Here, friends, a person has defilements but does not truly understand: 'There are defilements within me.' For such a person, this can be expected: 'He…
item.description:
Here, friends, a person has defilements but does not truly understand: 'There are defilements within me.' For such a person, this can be expected: 'He will not arouse desire, will not make effort, will not arouse energy to abandon those defilements. He will die while still having greed, still having hatred, still having delusion, still having defilements, still having a defiled mind.' Friends, just as a bronze bowl, brought from the market or from the smithy, covered with dust and grime, and its owner does not use it, does not clean it, and throws it into a dusty place. Friends, after a time, that bowl becomes even more defiled, even dustier.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 5 – Anaṅgaṇasutta

item.title: An Arahant bhikkhu, Who has done what had to be done, The taints destroyed, This body, his last body. Can he say: 'I speak'? Can…
item.description:
An Arahant bhikkhu,
Who has done what had to be done,
The taints destroyed,
This body, his last body.
Can he say:
'I speak'?
Can he say:
'They speak to me'?
( Blessed One ):
An Arahant bhikkhu,
Who has done what had to be done,
The taints destroyed,
This body, his last body.
He can say:
'I speak',
He can say:
'They speak to me'.
Skilfully knowing
Mere conventions in the world,
Using such conventions,
He would speak accordingly.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.25

item.title: ( Blessed One ): Thinking oneself equal, better, or worse, Conflict arises from that; One who is unmoved by these three, For them equal and…
item.description:
( Blessed One ):
Thinking oneself equal, better, or worse,
Conflict arises from that;
One who is unmoved by these three,
For them equal and better do not arise.

Give up reckoning,
Do not chase after vain thoughts,
Abandon all craving
For name-and-form in the world.
That one cuts the fetters,
Without worry, without craving.
Devas and humans,
In this world or the next,
In the deva realms,
Or in any abode,
Searching, they cannot find
The footprint of that one.

Throughout the world, do not do
Evil by body, speech, or mind.
Abandon all sensual desires,
Mindful, with clear comprehension,
Without torturing the body,
Vain and unbeneficial.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.20

item.description:
Elder Samiddatta:

The five aggregates are fully known,
Standing with roots cut off.
The end of suffering is attained; I have attained the destruction of taints.

From: Theragāthā 1.90

item.title: One who dwells in a view, considering it supreme, Placing it highest in the world, Says all others are inferior, Thus he does not transcend…
item.description:
One who dwells in a view, considering it supreme,
Placing it highest in the world,
Says all others are inferior,
Thus he does not transcend disputes.

When he sees a gain for himself in what is seen, heard,
Virtue, observance, or feeling,
There he grasps, he considers others as inferior.

The skilled say that is a bond — relying on which one regards others as inferior.
Therefore, a bhikkhu should not rely on what is seen, heard, felt, or observance.

Should not construct a view in the world by knowledge or by virtue,
Nor consider oneself equal or inferior;
Not thinking 'superior' or 'inferior'.

Having abandoned the self, not grasping anything,
Not depending on knowledge, not following factions,
Not holding to any view at all.

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.5

item.title: And, bhikkhus, what are the things to be fully understood? Form, bhikkhus, is a thing to be fully understood; feeling is a thing to be…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, what are the things to be fully understood? Form, bhikkhus, is a thing to be fully understood; feeling is a thing to be fully understood; perception is a thing to be fully understood; formations are things to be fully understood; consciousness is a thing to be fully understood. These, bhikkhus, are the things to be fully understood. And, bhikkhus, what is full understanding? The destruction of greed, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion, bhikkhus, is called full understanding.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.23

item.title: - Bhikkhus, form is suffering, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form,…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, form is suffering, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form, does not delight in future form, and for present form practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation. Bhikkhus, feeling is suffering ... perception is suffering ... formations are suffering ... Bhikkhus, consciousness is suffering, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past consciousness, does not delight in future consciousness, and for present consciousness practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.10

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, a person is shot with a dart, and then they shoot him with a second dart. Thus, bhikkhus, that person experiences the…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, a person is shot with a dart, and then they shoot him with a second dart. Thus, bhikkhus, that person experiences the feeling of both darts. So too, bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person, when touched by a painful feeling, sorrows, grieves, laments, beats his breast, and becomes confused. That person experiences two feelings: a bodily feeling and a mental feeling. Touched by that painful feeling, he feels aversion. Because he feels aversion towards that painful feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion towards painful feeling persists. Touched by that painful feeling, he delights in sensual pleasure. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, the unlearned ordinary person does not know any escape from painful feeling other than sensual pleasure. Delighting in that sensual pleasure, the underlying tendency to lust for pleasant feeling persists. He does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of those feelings. Because he does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of those feelings, the underlying tendency to ignorance for neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling persists. If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is bound. If he feels a painful feeling, he feels it as one who is bound. If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is bound. Bhikkhus, this is called an unlearned ordinary person who is bound by birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is bound by suffering.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 36.6
